correctness.rationale: Subtract vertex p-heat equations to obtain a_i′=φ_p(a_{i+1})+φ_p(a_{i-1})−2φ_p(a_i) for cyclic edge gradients ∑a_i=0. Monotonicity of φ_p and coordinate maximum principle give single-input L contraction. For p=2 the difference edge flow is linear heat; for n=3 the cycle equals complete graph and oscillation of two-solution vertex differences contracts by comparison. For n≥4 the explicit zero-sum base a=(1,R,−(R+n−2),1,…,1) and direction b=(1,1,−1,0,…,0,−1) have L(b)=1. The first-edge derivative of normalized two-solution symmetric perturbations tends to (p−1)(R^{p−2}−3). Choose R→∞ for p>2 or R↓0 for p<2 to make it arbitrarily positive, then choose ε>0 sufficiently small, proving unbounded liminf initial rate. All base edge values are nonzero when differentiation is used. This says nothing about infinite gain at any fixed positive time.
